mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in the month prior to the decision is interpreted by markets as a signal of heightened risk aversion, which compresses equity discount rates and drives negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during high-rate periods when the trigger is met, with a p-value > 0.05 in a two-sample test.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS exceeding 10,000 jobs signals stronger labor market absorption, which reduces the cost of capital via expectations of wage growth and supports positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant correlation between PAYEMS momentum and SPX 60-day forward returns in the last 5 years (R-squared < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 growth outpaces CPIAUCSL inflation by more than 2% in a quarter, it indicates robust demand for goods and services, which anticipates a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is negative or the signal is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in 70% of such events.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO above 5% suggests weakening manufacturing capacity, which raises the cost of capital and predicts negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO declines are not followed by SPX declines in > 60% of cases (counterfactual simulation).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of FEDFUNDS above 4% and RSAFS falling below 500,000 suggest over-tightening, which amplifies volatility and produces negative 20-day returns in the next two months.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% for 2 consecutive months AND RSAFS < 500,000
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive or the interaction term is not significant (p > 0.05) in a Granger causality test.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained UNRATE below 3.5% for three months indicates labor market weakness, lowering equity valuations and forecasting negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive or UNRATE remains below 3.5% without SPX decline (non-causal relationship).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) grows faster than GDP (GDPC1) by at least 5% in a quarter, it signals excess demand that is not price-stamped, leading to positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is negative or the interaction is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a rolling regression window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising), the combination of high FEDFUNDS and low UNRATE produces a regime-specific negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return, regardless of other signals.
candidate_trigger: regime:monetary tightening AND FEDFUNDS rising AND UNRATE < 4%
failure_condition: In tightening regimes, 20-day returns are positive or the interaction effect is not robust (p > 0.05 in a regime-stratified model).
